As the yolk-sac larva transitions toward exogenous feeding, a period of intense somatic growth ensues, with individuals accumulating mass through active foraging on zooplankton and detrital aggregates. Sexual maturation in Tigris bream is attained at a body size well below the species' ultimate dimensions, a pattern common among freshwater leuciscines. At this pubertal length (11.4 cm) [Lp = 11.4 cm], the corresponding wet weight of the fish is computed to be approximately 13 grams [Wwp = approximately 13 grams], derived from the same allometric equation that scales mass from length. The complete life cycle of Tigris bream proceeds at the pace dictated by the thermal regime of its lotic environment. Under laboratory conditions that mimic the annual temperature profile of the Tigris River, at a mean annual water temperature of 18 °C [T = 18 °C], the species exhibits a maximum recorded lifespan of 15 years [am = 15 years]. The interplay between size at maturity and maximum attainable size shapes the reproductive strategy of this cyprinid.
